title: where the required note shape is defined, and how it reaches every surface
summary: There is exactly ONE definition of what a note must contain — hooks/note-shape.mjs — and it lives in hooks/ rather than src/ because the capture hooks are plain .mjs that run straight from the package and never import from dist/; the TypeScript side reaches INTO hooks/ instead (the pattern lint.ts already uses with ignore.mjs), which is what lets one file serve the hook, the CLI and the MCP server. Adding a requirement is one NOTE_CHECKS entry and it reaches all five consumers at once: the write guide, the capture prompt's inlined shapes, the MCP kb_write description, the write-time warning, and kb repair's detection. Each entry carries TWO predicates on purpose — missingInSpec reads the JSON an agent just sent, missingInNote reads the folded note on disk; they cannot be collapsed, so they sit adjacent and a change to what 'missing' means has to be made in both, in view of each other. Verified this session: tsc's rootDir does NOT reject the cross-directory import (a .d.mts beside the .mjs supplies the types), and vitest imports the same file from both TS and .mjs test code.

steps.role: the single table plus its renderers
renders the guide and the write-time warning from checksForSpec
renders shapesBlock({compact:true}) inline — the copy that used to drift
kb_write description injects requiredFieldsLine(); this copy never said aliases at all
runs missingInNote over the folded notebook

invariants: Hooks NEVER import from dist/ — a shared table must live in hooks/ or the capture prompt cannot see it.
Renderings may differ in prose (compact drops it) but never in fields; tests/kb-shape-parity.test.ts asserts every required field appears in the example an agent copies.
A shipped `check` id is never removed — kb repair --json consumers filter by it; retire one by making its predicate always false.
missingInSpec and missingInNote read different shapes and cannot be merged; both live in the same entry so neither is edited alone.

title: where the required note shape is defined, and how it reaches every surface
invariants: Every write-time WARN is judged against the FOLDED note, never the record just sent — `op: put` appends and the fold merges, so a partial update omits fields it still has. Both call sites (src/kb/cli.ts and src/server/mcp.ts) load the folded note and must pass it to every warning; a warning that takes only the spec will misfire on updates.
